summary: Bakker–Klingler–Tsimerman show that arithmetic quotients carry a natural R_alg-definable structure, that period maps of polarized integral variations of Hodge structure are R_an,exp-definable (Theorem 1.3), and deduce, with the definable Chow theorem, that the components of the Hodge locus are algebraic (Theorem 1.6), a new proof of Cattani–Deligne–Kaplan. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-nine findings are recorded, with the official 2023 erratum covering E5–E7. Theorem 4.1 as printed (without shrinking the polydisk) is false (E1), though Theorem 1.3 is unaffected. Not formalised.

items.name: Existing pure Hodge structure
items.statement: On a complex vector space W with conjugation ω, a weight-k pure Hodge structure is an exhaustive decreasing filtration F with F^p complementary to the conjugate of F^(k+1−p). The integral specialization uses a lattice and its complexification.

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.pieceDecomposition
api.statement: Recover F^a as the direct sum of H^(p,k−p) with p≥a.

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.conjugatePiece
api.statement: Conjugation sends H^(p,k−p) to H^(k−p,p).

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.shiftWeight
api.statement: A Tate shift by m has weight k−2m and filtration F^(p+m).

uses.how: Specify fibrewise opposed filtrations with the same weight.

items.name: Existing module-valued local system
items.statement: An R-module local coefficient system on a topological space X is a functor from its fundamental groupoid to ModuleCat R. For the integral PVHS consumer the fibres must additionally be finite free Z-modules; the generic carrier alone imposes neither freeness nor finiteness.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.transportIdentity
api.statement: Transport along the constant path is the identity.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.transportCompose
api.statement: Transport along a concatenation is the composite in the selected path convention.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.finiteFreeFibres
api.statement: A PVHS adapter explicitly requires each integral fibre finite free; this is additional to LocalCoefficientSystem.

uses.how: Supply flat integral fibres and monodromy transport.

items.name: Existing polarized period-domain point
items.statement: Fix a finite free Z-lattice V, its complexification, integral bilinear form Q, weight k and a finite-support symmetric Hodge type. A point is a Hodge filtration of that type polarized by Q. This carrier does not provide topology or a complex manifold.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.filtrationExt
api.statement: Two period points with equal filtrations are equal.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.hodgeRanks
api.statement: The prescribed Hodge dimensions sum to the complex dimension.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.fixedPolarization
api.statement: The same input integral form polarizes every point; changing the form changes the parameter, not a field of the point.

uses.how: Retain the existing fixed-polarization carrier under the manifold realization.

items.name: Existing Weil operator
items.statement: For a weight-k pure Hodge structure, C is the complex-linear endomorphism acting by i^(p−q) on H^(p,q), where p+q=k.

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.onPiece
api.statement: C acts on H^(p,q) by i^(p−q).

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.square
api.statement: C²=(−1)^k times the identity in weight k.

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.realCompatibility
api.statement: C commutes with conjugation on the real form.

uses.how: Convert polarized Hodge pieces into the metric.

items.name: Existing Hermitian Hodge form
items.statement: For a polarization Q, the pinned library form is h_lib(u,v)=Q(C(conj u),v), conjugate-linear in u and linear in v. It equals the complex conjugate of the paper convention h_BKT(u,v)=Q(Cu,conj v). Diagonal real norms agree.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.conventionConjugate
api.statement: h_lib(u,v)=conj(h_BKT(u,v)) with the displayed Weil and polarization conventions.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.diagonalAgreement
api.statement: h_lib(u,u)=h_BKT(u,u) is real.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.sesquilinearity
api.statement: h_lib(au,bv)=conj(a)b h_lib(u,v).

uses.how: Use diagonal norms while reconciling conjugation conventions.

items.name: Existing positivity of the Hodge form
items.statement: For any polarization P and nonzero vector u in the complexification, P.hodgeForm(u,u)>0. In particular its real restriction is positive definite. Nonzero u is essential.

items.name: Existing rational mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: On compatible rational and complex models of an integral module, a mixed Hodge structure consists of a finite increasing rational weight filtration W and finite decreasing complex Hodge filtration F for which gr^W_k with its induced F is pure of weight k.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.gradedPure
api.statement: The k-th rational weight graded with its induced F is pure of weight k.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.rationalWeight
api.statement: Complex weights are complexifications of rational subspaces and are conjugation-stable.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.pureAsMixed
api.statement: A pure weight-k structure defines a mixed structure with only gr_k nonzero.

uses.how: Package the shifted monodromy filtration and limiting F.

items.name: Existing Deligne bigrading
items.statement: For a mixed Hodge structure, I^(p,q)=(F^p∩W_(p+q))∩((conj F^q∩W_(p+q))+Σ_(j≥2)(conj F^(q−j+1)∩W_(p+q−j))). The weights here use the actual mixed weight; centered monodromy indices require a shift by the pure weight.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.recoverF
api.statement: F^a is the sum of I^(p,q) for p≥a.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.recoverW
api.statement: W_k is the sum of I^(p,q) for p+q≤k.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.conjugateModuloLower
api.statement: conj I^(p,q) equals I^(q,p) modulo pieces with first index<q and second index<p.

uses.how: Import the one-filtration decomposition without assuming the multi-filtration extension.

items.name: Existing direct-sum and filtration recovery
items.statement: The I^(p,q) form an internal direct sum of the underlying complex vector space. F^p∩W_k is the sum of the pieces I^(r,s) with r≥p and r+s≤k. This concerns one mixed Hodge structure, not simultaneous splittings of several monodromy filtrations.

items.name: Existing finite exponential of a nilpotent
items.statement: For a nilpotent a in a Q-algebra with a^m=0, exp_nil(a)=Σ_(0≤j<m) a^j/j!. Commuting nilpotents a,b satisfy exp_nil(a+b)=exp_nil(a)exp_nil(b). The analytic exponential comparison is a separate interface if needed.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.truncate
api.statement: If N^m=0, exp_nil(zN)=Σ_(j<m) z^j N^j/j!.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.commutingSum
api.statement: For commuting nilpotents A,B, exp_nil(A+B)=exp_nil(A)exp_nil(B).

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.inverse
api.statement: exp_nil(N)exp_nil(−N)=1.

uses.how: Use a finite algebraic polynomial for monodromy twists.

items.name: Expansions of the ordered real field
items.statement: A structure consists of Boolean algebras of subsets of R^n containing semialgebraic sets and closed under products and coordinate projections; parameters from R are allowed. A function is definable when its graph is definable.

api.name: BKT.RealDefinableStructure.semialgebraicInclusion
api.statement: Every semialgebraic set with real parameters is definable.

api.name: BKT.RealDefinableStructure.project
api.statement: Coordinate projections of definable sets are definable.

api.name: BKT.RealDefinableStructure.boolean
api.statement: Finite unions and complements are definable in each fixed arity.

uses.how: Express graph images and pullbacks by projections and Boolean operations.

items.name: O-minimality
items.statement: An expansion of the ordered real field is o-minimal if every definable subset of R is a finite union of points and intervals.

api.name: BKT.OMinimal.oneDimensionalDecomposition
api.statement: A definable subset of R is a finite union of points and intervals.

api.name: BKT.OMinimal.discreteFinite
api.statement: A definable discrete subset of R is finite.

api.name: BKT.OMinimal.reduct
api.statement: An ordered-field reduct of an o-minimal expansion is o-minimal.

uses.how: Exclude infinite discrete definable fibres.

items.name: Restricted analytic functions
items.statement: A real function is restricted analytic when it agrees on a fixed compact box with an analytic function on an open neighborhood of that box and is zero outside it. Rescaling compact boxes does not change the generated structure.

api.name: BKT.RestrictedAnalytic.bufferRestriction
api.statement: An analytic function on a neighborhood of a closed box gives a restricted analytic function on that box.

api.name: BKT.RestrictedAnalytic.rescaleBox
api.statement: Affine rescaling between compact boxes preserves restricted analyticity.

api.name: BKT.RestrictedAnalytic.complexComponents
api.statement: Real and imaginary parts of a holomorphic function on a buffered compact polydisk are R_an-definable.

uses.how: Restrict trigonometric functions and the untwisted period map on buffered compact boxes.

items.name: The structures R_alg, R_an, R_exp and R_an,exp
items.statement: R_alg is the real semialgebraic structure; R_an adds restricted real analytic functions; R_exp adds real exponential; R_an,exp adds both. Inclusions of structures preserve definability; none identifies the Borel–Serre and algebraic structures without a comparison.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.algebraicToAnalytic
api.statement: R_alg-definable sets are R_an-definable.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.analyticToCombined
api.statement: R_an-definability implies R_an,exp-definability.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.realExpDefinable
api.statement: The real exponential is definable in R_exp and R_an,exp.

uses.how: Keep analytic and exponential languages and their inclusions explicit.

items.name: O-minimality of the required real expansions
items.statement: R_alg, R_an, R_exp and R_an,exp are o-minimal. The R_an case uses Gabrielov/van den Dries and the combined case uses van den Dries–Miller; the combined assertion is not inferred merely from o-minimality of its two reducts.

items.name: Definable manifolds with finite atlas
items.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space has a definable manifold structure if it has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods with definable chart images, overlaps and transition homeomorphisms. Structures are identified when mixed transitions are definable.

api.name: BKT.FiniteDefinableAtlas.compatibleRefinement
api.statement: Finite definable refinements produce the same definable subsets.

api.name: BKT.FiniteDefinableAtlas.graphCriterion
api.statement: A map is definable iff its graph is definable in all pairs of charts.

api.name: BKT.FiniteDefinableAtlas.finiteGlue
api.statement: Compatible definable maps on a finite definable cover glue definably.

uses.how: Provide finite graph checks independent of charts.

items.name: Definable images, pullbacks and finite gluing
items.statement: Graphs of maps between finite definable atlases define maps independently of the atlas. Composition, finite products, images and inverse images are definable; maps that agree on a finite definable cover glue definably. Descent through a definable surjection holds by projecting the graph of the composite.

items.name: Real analytic manifolds with corners
items.statement: Charts are homeomorphisms from relatively open subsets of [0,∞)^r×R^(n−r) to open subsets of a paracompact Hausdorff space. Transitions and their inverses extend real analytically to ambient open neighborhoods. Weakly analytic maps are continuous maps satisfying this extension property in charts.

api.name: BKT.AnalyticCorners.interior
api.statement: The depth-zero locus is a real analytic n-manifold.

api.name: BKT.AnalyticCorners.ambientExtension
api.statement: Each chart transition has an analytic extension on an ambient neighborhood.

api.name: BKT.AnalyticCorners.depthInvariant
api.statement: The number of local boundary hyperplanes through a point is chart-independent.

uses.how: Use ambient analytic extensions and compact shrinking to build restricted-analytic charts.

items.name: Boundary with local branches
items.statement: The boundary of an n-manifold with corners consists of pairs (x,b), where b is a local codimension-one boundary component at x. It is an (n−1)-manifold with corners with a weakly analytic immersion i_X to X; i_X need not be injective at corners.
items.locator: Appendix A.1; A.1 prints dimension n, corrected to n − 1 as in the proof of Proposition A.2 (sourceIssues E4)

api.name: BKT.CornerBoundary.dimension
api.statement: The boundary has dimension n−1 when n≥1.

api.name: BKT.CornerBoundary.branchImmersion
api.statement: The map (x,b)↦x is weakly analytic and locally an immersion.

api.name: BKT.CornerBoundary.fibreDepth
api.statement: The fibre over x has one element for each local boundary branch, hence cardinality depth(x).

uses.how: Distinguish local branches from their coincident image at a corner.

items.name: Definable manifolds with corners
items.statement: Use finite atlases as for finite-definable-atlas, now with definable relatively open orthant domains; overlap homeomorphisms are definable. Definable subsets and graphs are tested in every chart. No ambient smoothness is built into this topological definability carrier.

api.name: BKT.DefinableCorners.orthantCharts
api.statement: Each chart image is relatively open in a definable orthant.

api.name: BKT.DefinableCorners.definableInterior
api.statement: The locus where all boundary coordinates are positive is definable.

api.name: BKT.DefinableCorners.boundaryCharts
api.statement: Restricting one coordinate to zero constructs the finite definable boundary atlas with its branch labels.

uses.how: Encode the finite atlas obtained from compact analytic corners.

items.name: Compact analytic corners admit a canonical R_an structure
items.statement: A compact real analytic manifold with corners admits an R_an-definable structure obtained from any finite buffered analytic chart cover. Two such constructions have definable identity maps, giving a canonical structure. Compatibility is not asserted for arbitrary nonbuffered analytic charts.
items.note: Compatibility is asserted for buffered finite analytic subatlases; an arbitrary nonbuffered analytic chart need not be globally subanalytic. SourceIssues E17 records the missing buffer in the printed argument.

items.name: Definability of boundary immersion and interior
items.statement: For compact analytic X with corners and its canonical R_an structure, the boundary-branch immersion i_X is R_an-definable, and X minus its image is a definable manifold.

items.name: Cartan involutions and maximal compact subgroups
items.statement: For a connected real reductive group, a Cartan involution determines its maximal compact fixed subgroup K and a Cartan decomposition. In the arithmetic application choose K containing the given connected compact subgroup M; its conjugates give the symmetric space of maximal compact subgroups.

api.name: BKT.CartanMaximalCompact.fixedSubgroup
api.statement: K is the fixed subgroup of the chosen Cartan involution.

api.name: BKT.CartanMaximalCompact.conjugateChoice
api.statement: Conjugation by g transports K and its Cartan involution together.

api.name: BKT.CartanMaximalCompact.containsCompact
api.statement: For a compact subgroup M in a real linear reductive group, choose maximal compact K containing M.

uses.how: Retain K and its Cartan involution as parameters of every Siegel construction.

items.name: Arithmetic quotient with chosen compact data
items.statement: Let Gbold be connected semisimple over Q, G=Gbold(R)^+, Γ⊂Gbold(Q)∩G torsion-free arithmetic, M⊂G connected compact, and K⊃M maximal compact. The underlying quotient is Γ\G/M; its definable and Borel–Serre structures retain K as data. Use neat Γ when invoking the boundary freeness theorem.

api.name: BKT.ArithmeticQuotient.quotientWellDefined
api.statement: The class of h identifies γhm with h for γ∈Γ and m∈M.

api.name: BKT.ArithmeticQuotient.fixedKParameter
api.statement: The definable structure is indexed by a maximal compact K containing M.

api.name: BKT.ArithmeticQuotient.neatUpgrade
api.statement: A finite-index neat subgroup yields a finite covering of the torsion-free quotient; boundary freeness uses neatness explicitly.

uses.how: Specify the quotient set and topology before constructing its fixed-K definable structure.

items.name: Morphisms compatible with chosen maximal compacts
items.statement: A morphism from (Γ′,G′,M′,K′) to (Γ,G,M,K) is induced by a Q-group map φ and g∈G, via Γ′h′M′↦Γφ(h′)gM, with φΓ′⊂Γ, φM′⊂gMg⁻¹, φK′⊂gKg⁻¹, and the Cartan involution for gKg⁻¹ stabilizing dφ(g′). Definability is a conclusion, not an extra assumed property of this data.

api.name: BKT.CompatibleMorphism.quotientMap
api.statement: The two level/stabilizer inclusions make [h′]↦[φ(h′)g] well defined.

api.name: BKT.CompatibleMorphism.cartanImageStable
api.statement: The chosen target Cartan involution stabilizes the image Lie algebra.

api.name: BKT.CompatibleMorphism.translateCompact
api.statement: Right translation by g identifies the compact data gKg⁻¹ and K without requiring Int(g) to be defined over Q.

uses.how: Supply exactly the corrected hypotheses needed by rational Siegel containment.

items.name: Rational parabolic and horospherical data
items.statement: For a rational parabolic P of Gbold, let N_P be its unipotent radical and L_P its Levi quotient. Let A_P be the positive real component of the maximal Q-split central torus of L_P, and M_P the intersection of kernels of squares of its Q-characters on real points. A chosen K selects a Cartan-stable real Levi lift, not necessarily defined over Q, and G=N_P A_P M_P K in horospherical coordinates.

api.name: BKT.RationalParabolicData.leviQuotient
api.statement: P/N_P is the rational reductive Levi quotient.

api.name: BKT.RationalParabolicData.cartanLift
api.statement: K specifies a real Cartan-stable lift of that quotient.

api.name: BKT.RationalParabolicData.horosphericalCoordinates
api.statement: Every g admits the N_P A_P M_P K factorization with the stated stabilizers.

uses.how: Choose the rational and real pieces of horospherical coordinates without conflating them.

items.name: Positive root coordinates and truncations
items.statement: Let Δ be the rational simple roots on A_P acting on Lie(N_P). Their positive evaluations give A_P≅(R_>0)^r. For t>0, A_(P,t)={a:α(a)>t for all α∈Δ}; the inverse-root map e_P(a)=(α(a)⁻¹)_α identifies the chamber with a bounded corner approaching coordinate zero at infinity.

api.name: BKT.PositiveRootCone.inverseRootPositive
api.statement: For a∈A_P, every inverse-root coordinate is positive.

api.name: BKT.PositiveRootCone.coneImage
api.statement: A_(P,t) maps to coordinates strictly between 0 and 1/t.

api.name: BKT.PositiveRootCone.rankZero
api.statement: For an empty simple-root set the cone condition is vacuous and the corner factor is a point.

uses.how: Turn cusp growth into boundary coordinates.

items.name: Semialgebraic Siegel set for fixed K
items.statement: For the fixed Cartan/Levi data of P and K, a Siegel set is U A_(P,t) W with t>0 and relatively compact semialgebraic U⊂N_P, W⊂M_PK; open versions give interior covers and compact closures give proper relations. Its image in G/M is a Siegel set associated to the same K.

api.name: BKT.SiegelSet.semialgebraic
api.statement: A Siegel set with semialgebraic relatively compact U,W is semialgebraic.

api.name: BKT.SiegelSet.coneMonotonicity
api.statement: Increasing t shrinks the Siegel set with U,W fixed.

api.name: BKT.SiegelSet.quotientImage
api.statement: The image under G→G/M is semialgebraic in the homogeneous model.

uses.how: Use fixed-K sets in the reduction and quotient arguments.

items.name: Translation and conjugation rules with compact data
items.statement: Conjugation by g carries a Siegel set for (P,K) to one for (gPg⁻¹,gKg⁻¹). Right translation by real g carries the fixed-P construction to compact g⁻¹Kg; rational left translations can be represented as Siegel sets with the original K and a changed rational parabolic. Retain the coordinate identifications in each rule.

items.name: Finite arithmetic cover by fixed-K Siegel sets
items.statement: There are finitely many Γ-conjugacy classes of rational parabolics and finitely many associated semialgebraic Siegel sets, all using the chosen K, whose images cover Γ\G/M.

items.name: Finite arithmetic overlaps of Siegel sets
items.statement: For any two Siegel sets S₁,S₂ associated to the same K, the set of γ∈Γ with γS₁∩S₂ nonempty is finite. The property extends to relatively compact closures of their unipotent and Levi factors.

items.name: Separation of inequivalent cusps
items.statement: If P₁ and P₂ are not Γ-conjugate, then for fixed bounded U_i,W_i and sufficiently large truncation parameters t_i, γS₁∩S₂ is empty for every γ∈Γ. All Siegel data use one K.

items.name: Deep self-intersections come from the parabolic
items.statement: For fixed U,W and sufficiently large t, a Siegel set S for P and K satisfies γS∩S=∅ whenever γ∈Γ\(Γ∩P).

items.name: Deep corners for distinct parabolics separate
items.statement: For distinct rational parabolics P₁≠P₂ and fixed bounded factors using one K, the corresponding Siegel sets are disjoint once both truncation parameters are sufficiently large.

items.name: Semialgebraic model of G/M
items.statement: For G as above and connected compact M, the homogeneous space G/M admits a semialgebraic model inducing its quotient topology, with semialgebraic projection G→G/M and semialgebraic left G-action. Its construction is independent of the later choice of K.
items.note: Corrected E8 and E9. The orbit map itself separates right cosets; subsequently taking invariants for the left M-action destroys this separation.

api.name: BKT.CompactHomogeneousModel.projection
api.statement: G→G/M is semialgebraic and has the quotient topology.

api.name: BKT.CompactHomogeneousModel.leftAction
api.statement: The G-action on the model is semialgebraic.

api.name: BKT.CompactHomogeneousModel.orbitEquality
api.statement: Two points of G have the same image iff their quotient lies in M.

uses.how: Supply semialgebraic orbits before taking the arithmetic quotient.

items.name: Semialgebraic quotient of a definably proper equivalence relation
items.statement: For a closed semialgebraic equivalence relation on a semialgebraic set whose coordinate projections are definably proper in the sense of van den Dries Chapter10, the topological quotient has the corresponding semialgebraic quotient structure. For a locally free étale relation with manifold local slices, refine to a finite definable manifold atlas.
items.note: The source theorem and its exact properness convention need original-book audit; this is an explicit open interface, not a claimed general quotient theorem without those hypotheses.

items.name: Borel–Serre corner for a rational parabolic
items.statement: For fixed K and rational P, form N_P×[0,∞)^Δ×M_PK using inverse-simple-root coordinates. Its interior is the corresponding horospherical model of G, and its zero coordinate faces record larger parabolics via their incidence relations.

api.name: BKT.BsCorner.interiorCoordinates
api.statement: The positive-coordinate locus identifies with G through the horospherical coordinates.

api.name: BKT.BsCorner.faceLabel
api.statement: Vanishing-coordinate subsets select the corresponding rational-parabolic boundary face.

api.name: BKT.BsCorner.weakAnalyticOverlap
api.statement: Transition maps between incident corners extend analytically to ambient neighborhoods on their domains.

uses.how: Match inverse-root boundary charts with rational parabolic incidence.

items.name: Borel–Serre partial compactification for fixed K
items.statement: Glue the corners for rational parabolics to G, with boundary pieces N_P×M_PK for proper P. The topology and real analytic corner structure depend on K. The symmetric-space quotient M=K must agree with the existing ALS.2 construction.

api.name: BKT.GeneralBsSpace.interiorEmbedding
api.statement: G embeds as the open depth-zero locus of the glued space.

api.name: BKT.GeneralBsSpace.boundaryStratum
api.statement: The stratum for P is N_P×M_PK.

api.name: BKT.GeneralBsSpace.symmetricSpecialization
api.statement: Taking the right quotient by M=K agrees with the ALS.2 Borel–Serre space.

uses.how: Extend the existing symmetric construction to the required compact stabilizer quotient.

items.name: Embedding of every Borel–Serre corner
items.statement: The horospherical identification of G extends to an embedding N_P×[0,∞)^Δ×M_PK into the partial compactification. Sets U×closure(e_P(A_(P,t)))×W give neighborhood charts at the P-boundary.

items.name: Extended commuting arithmetic and compact actions
items.statement: Left multiplication by Gbold(Q)∩G and right multiplication by K extend to commuting weakly real analytic actions on the fixed-K partial compactification. Restrict the latter to M⊂K.

items.name: Compact analytic corner quotient
items.statement: For neat arithmetic Γ and connected compact M⊂K, the Γ×M action gives a free proper quotient Γ\Gbar^BS_K/M, a compact real analytic manifold with corners whose interior is Γ\G/M. General torsion-free interior statements are separated from neat boundary inputs.

items.name: Finite relation on Siegel closures
items.statement: On the disjoint union of closures of finitely many fixed-K Siegel sets covering Γ\G/M, relate x and y when γx=y for some γ∈Γ. Only finitely many γ occur for each pair of sets; the relation is semialgebraic and has the properness needed for the quotient theorem.

api.name: BKT.SiegelEquivalenceRelation.finiteWitnesses
api.statement: For each pair of fixed-K pieces only a finite subset of Γ can identify their points.

api.name: BKT.SiegelEquivalenceRelation.equivalenceLaws
api.statement: The orbit relation on the tagged union is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

api.name: BKT.SiegelEquivalenceRelation.definableProper
api.statement: The chosen closure presentation has a semialgebraic proper relation; use a quotient theorem with that exact hypothesis.

uses.how: Present the arithmetic quotient through finitely many definable pieces.

items.name: Definable structure on an arithmetic quotient with K
items.statement: For every torsion-free arithmetic Γ and connected compact M⊂K as above, Γ\G/M has an R_alg-definable manifold structure characterized by definability of π restricted to every semialgebraic Siegel set associated to K. A finite union of such sets is a semialgebraic fundamental set on which π is definable.

items.name: Compatibility with the analytic Borel–Serre structure
items.statement: At neat level and for the same K on both constructions, the R_an expansion of arithmetic-definable-structure equals the structure induced on the interior of Γ\Gbar^BS_K/M by its compact real analytic corner atlas.

items.name: Corrected containment of subgroup Siegel sets
items.statement: Let H⊂G be reductive Q-groups and S_H a Siegel set for a triple (P_H,A_H,K_H). For a fixed maximal compact K_G containing K_H, assume its Cartan involution stabilizes the split torus A_H. Then S_H is contained in finitely many G(Q)-translates of a Siegel set for K_G. The triples can be chosen with R_u(P_H)⊂R_u(P_G) and A_H=A_G∩H.
items.locator: Orr–Schnell2023 Theorem1; replacing the fixed-K use of originalTheorem3.2

items.name: Subgroup stability is a sufficient stronger condition
items.statement: If K_H⊂K_G and θ_(K_G) stabilizes H, its restriction is the Cartan involution for H and stabilizes the split torus of an H-Siegel triple. Thus the corrected containment theorem applies. The converse implication from torus stability to subgroup stability is false.

items.name: Rational Siegel intersection with a subgroup
items.statement: Let H⊂G be reductive over Q, K_H=K_G∩H(R) maximal compact, and assume every K_H-Siegel set lies in finitely many G(Q)-translates of some K_G-Siegel set. For every K_G-Siegel set S_G there are a K_H-Siegel set S_H and finite F⊂H(Q) with S_G∩H(R)⊂F S_H.
items.note: The forward containment hypothesis is part of the statement. Borel–Harish-Chandra7.5 for real Siegel domains is not substituted here.

items.name: Definability of compatible arithmetic morphisms
items.statement: Every compatible-morphism is R_alg-definable between the fixed-K arithmetic quotient structures.
items.note: The original §3.2 product equality for arithmetic quotients needs finite-index and compact-stabilizer bookkeeping; it is not adopted literally.

items.name: Arithmetic Hecke correspondence
items.statement: For g∈Gbold(Q)∩G, the commensurable groups Γ and g⁻¹Γg have finite-index intersection. The correspondence from Γ\G/M through this intersection is given by the natural projection and left multiplication by g followed by projection.

api.name: BKT.HeckeCorrespondence.intersectionLevel
api.statement: Γ∩g⁻¹Γg has finite index in both arithmetic groups.

api.name: BKT.HeckeCorrespondence.firstLeg
api.statement: The first leg is the quotient projection from the intersection level.

api.name: BKT.HeckeCorrespondence.secondLeg
api.statement: The second leg sends the class of h to the class of gh and uses rational Int(g) with the corresponding right translation.

uses.how: Prove definability of both finite correspondence legs with the corrected morphism contract.

items.name: Semialgebraicity of Hecke correspondences
items.statement: The two maps of hecke-correspondence are finite local covering maps and R_alg-definable for the chosen arithmetic quotient structure. The conjugation morphism (Int(g),g) satisfies the corrected compact compatibility.

items.name: Dependence on maximal compact is real
items.statement: For G=SL₂ and M={1}, distinct maximal compacts K_x,K_y yield distinct definable structures on Γ\G. The overlap fibre product of corresponding Siegel sets has infinitely many connected components, excluding a definable identity map in an o-minimal structure.

items.name: Compact inclusion alone does not imply Siegel containment
items.statement: There are reductive, and also semisimple, rational subgroup inclusions with K_H⊂K_G for which an H-Siegel set is not covered by finitely many rational translates of K_G-Siegel sets. Therefore the Cartan compatibility cannot be deleted from the definable-morphism interface.

items.name: Polarized integral variation of Hodge structure
items.statement: A pure weight-k integral variation on a complex manifold S consists of a finite free Z-local system, its holomorphic complex bundle with flat connection, a holomorphic decreasing filtration with fibrewise pure Hodge structures, a flat integral polarization, and Griffiths transversality ∇F^p⊂F^(p−1)⊗Ω¹_S.

api.name: BKT.PolarizedVariation.flatPolarization
api.statement: Parallel transport preserves the fixed integral bilinear form.

api.name: BKT.PolarizedVariation.griffiths
api.statement: The connection sends F^p into F^(p−1)⊗Ω¹.

api.name: BKT.PolarizedVariation.holomorphicPullback
api.statement: Holomorphic pullback preserves an integral polarized variation and its weight.

uses.how: Derive horizontal holomorphic period maps from the planned general VHS definition.

items.name: Complex period domain and compact dual
items.statement: For fixed polarized lattice and Hodge numbers, the period-domain point carrier is realized as an open real-semialgebraic orbit D=G/M in a complex flag variety Dcheck, with its complex manifold structure and horizontal tangent subbundle. In general M is compact but not maximal compact, so D need not be Hermitian symmetric. The G_C-action on Dcheck is algebraic.

api.name: BKT.GeneralPeriodDomain.pointEquivalence
api.statement: The analytic domain has the existing PeriodDomain.Point carrier with the fixed lattice/form/type.

api.name: BKT.GeneralPeriodDomain.compactDualAction
api.statement: The complexified algebraic group acts algebraically on the flag compact dual.

api.name: BKT.GeneralPeriodDomain.horizontalTangent
api.statement: The horizontal subbundle is the degree −1 filtration-lowering part of the tangent space.

uses.how: Provide the complex geometry absent from the built point carrier.

items.name: Connected Hodge datum and canonical compact
items.statement: A pure polarizable rational Hodge datum is a rational reductive group together with the relevant connected conjugacy class of a Hodge homomorphism. On its adjoint semisimple group the Hodge metric on the Lie algebra defines a canonical maximal compact K_t and the Weil operator defines its Cartan involution. The centralizer M of the Hodge point is contained in K_t.

api.name: BKT.HodgeDatum.adjointCartan
api.statement: The Weil operator of the adjoint polarized Hodge structure induces the canonical Cartan involution.

api.name: BKT.HodgeDatum.stabilizerContained
api.statement: The point stabilizer M lies in its canonical maximal compact K_t.

api.name: BKT.HodgeDatum.hodgeMorphismsPreserve
api.statement: A morphism of Hodge data preserves the Cartan data and stabilizes the image Lie algebra under the target involution.

uses.how: Select the canonical Cartan involution on the adjoint Lie algebra.

items.name: Arithmetic Hodge manifold with canonical tame structure
items.statement: For a Hodge datum and a neat arithmetic subgroup Γ of its adjoint group, let Hod_Γ,t=Γ\D. Equip it with its complex analytic quotient and with the R_alg-definable structure associated to the canonical K_t. These structures coexist; Hod_Γ,t is not assumed algebraic.

api.name: BKT.HodgeManifold.analyticQuotient
api.statement: At neat level Γ acts freely and properly on D, giving the complex analytic quotient.

api.name: BKT.HodgeManifold.canonicalDefinable
api.statement: Use arithmetic-definable-structure with the Hodge-derived K_t.

api.name: BKT.HodgeManifold.levelChange
api.statement: Finite-index level changes give finite holomorphic definable maps.

uses.how: Use the canonical fixed-K arithmetic structure on a complex analytic target.

items.name: Period map of an integral variation
items.statement: A polarized integral variation determines a locally liftable holomorphic horizontal map into the appropriate arithmetic Hodge manifold after the finite étale level change needed for a torsion-free arithmetic target. On a simply connected open set the lift sends a flat marking to its Hodge filtration; changing the marking acts by monodromy.

api.name: BKT.PeriodMap.localLift
api.statement: A flat marking on a simply connected open set sends each fibre filtration to a period-domain point.

api.name: BKT.PeriodMap.deckEquivariance
api.statement: Changing a lift by a deck transformation acts through its integral monodromy.

api.name: BKT.PeriodMap.horizontalHolomorphic
api.statement: The local lifts and descended period map are holomorphic and horizontal.

uses.how: Relate the global map to monodromy-equivariant local lifts.

items.name: Hodge morphisms preserve the canonical compact data
items.statement: For a rational Hodge morphism φ with φ∘t′=g t g⁻¹ and φΓ′⊂Γ, the induced map of Lie algebras is a Hodge morphism. It sends K_(t′) into gK_tg⁻¹ and its image is stable under the latter Cartan involution. The resulting map of pure Hodge manifolds is R_alg-definable.

items.name: Finite buffered charts near a normal-crossing boundary
items.statement: A smooth complex quasi-projective S has a smooth projective compactification with simple normal-crossing boundary. A finite cover by sufficiently small coordinate polydisks, whose closures lie inside larger analytic coordinate neighborhoods, reduces the period-map problem to smaller punctured polydisks times disks.

items.name: Quasi-unipotence of local monodromy
items.statement: The integral monodromy operators of a polarized variation around the coordinates of a punctured polydisk commute and have roots of unity as eigenvalues. Finite coordinate power covers make all of them unipotent.
items.note: The lemma and proof were read; its horizontal metric-decrease input remains an original-source leaf.

items.name: Commuting nilpotent logarithms
items.statement: After unipotent reduction, N_i=log(T_i)=Σ_(j≥1)(−1)^(j+1)(T_i−1)^j/j is a finite nilpotent rational endomorphism. The N_i commute, preserve the polarization infinitesimally, and exp(N_i)=T_i.

api.name: BKT.MonodromyLogarithms.finiteLog
api.statement: If (T−1)^m=0 the displayed logarithm truncates before degree m.

api.name: BKT.MonodromyLogarithms.exponentialInverse
api.statement: exp_nil(log T)=T.

api.name: BKT.MonodromyLogarithms.commutingLogs
api.statement: Commuting unipotent T_i yield commuting nilpotent logarithms N_i.

uses.how: Polynomially untwist the unipotent deck transformations.

items.name: Nilpotent orbit and untwisted period map
items.statement: For a lift Φtilde on H^n with unipotent monodromy, Ψ(q)=exp(−Σz_iN_i)Φtilde(z), q_i=exp(2πiz_i), is single-valued into Dcheck. A nilpotent orbit is the horizontal map z↦exp(Σz_iN_i)F that lies in D whenever all imaginary coordinates are sufficiently large.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentOrbit.untwistedDescent
api.statement: exp(−Σz_iN_i)Φtilde(z) is invariant under integral shifts z_i↦z_i+1.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentOrbit.twistRecovery
api.statement: Φtilde(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)Ψ(q(z)).

api.name: BKT.NilpotentOrbit.deepPositivity
api.statement: A nilpotent orbit lies in D only after the stipulated lower bound on all imaginary coordinates.

uses.how: Separate the single-valued untwisted map from the limiting orbit.

items.name: Holomorphic extension of the untwisted map
items.statement: For a polarized variation on a punctured polydisk with unipotent monodromy, Ψ extends holomorphically to the full polydisk with values in Dcheck. Its limiting filtration F=Ψ(0) defines a nilpotent orbit. Auxiliary unpunctured variables are allowed on relatively compact subdisks.
items.note: The original statement was read; Schmid§8 proof is not fully audited.

items.name: Bounded-real-part sector and ordered sector
items.statement: For R,η>0 let H^n_(R,η)={z: |Re z_i|≤R and Im z_i≥η}. For local estimates use ordered sectors Σ_n={0<Re z_i<1, Im z₁≥⋯≥Im z_n>1}. Finitely many permutations cover the imaginary-order choices; finitely many overlapping real strips cover angular seams.

api.name: BKT.BoundedSector.imaginaryOrderCover
api.statement: The finitely many coordinate permutations cover all choices of imaginary-coordinate order.

api.name: BKT.BoundedSector.boundedTrig
api.statement: Sine and cosine of 2π Re z are restricted analytic on bounded real intervals.

api.name: BKT.BoundedSector.angularSeams
api.statement: A finite family of overlapping intervals covers one full turn without omitting the positive ray.

uses.how: Make real widths, cusp heights and finite permutations explicit.

items.name: Definability of the punctured-disk covering on a sector
items.statement: On a bounded real strip, z↦exp(2πiz) has R_an,exp-definable real and imaginary parts: e^(−2πy) times restricted sine and cosine in x. A finite set of overlapping strips covers the punctured disk of any fixed smaller radius.

items.name: Definability of the lifted local period map
items.statement: On a bounded-real sector mapping into a sufficiently small punctured polydisk, Φtilde(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)Ψ(q(z)) is R_an,exp-definable as a map to D. The nilpotent exponential is polynomial and Ψ is restricted analytic after shrinking.

items.name: Restricted-analytic coefficient and Laurent polynomial rings
items.statement: On an ordered sector Σ_n, let O be the real algebra of functions pulled back by q from real analytic functions on a neighborhood of a fixed closed polydisk. Let O[x,y,y⁻¹] be the algebra generated by x_i,y_i,y_i⁻¹; use its fraction field on common nonvanishing domains. Complex-valued entries are represented by real and imaginary parts.

api.name: BKT.RoughFunctionRings.coefficientPullback
api.statement: An analytic coefficient on a neighborhood of the closed polydisk pulls back along q.

api.name: BKT.RoughFunctionRings.laurentClosure
api.statement: The coefficient algebra with x_i,y_i,y_i⁻¹ is closed under sums and products.

api.name: BKT.RoughFunctionRings.nonzeroDomain
api.statement: A rational expression is evaluated only on its denominator-nonvanishing domain.

uses.how: Track analytic coefficients, polynomial growth and allowed denominators.

items.name: Roughly monomial function
items.statement: A positive function f in the rational function algebra on Σ_n is roughly monomial if some integer exponent vector s and constants 0<c≤C satisfy c∏y_i^s_i≤f≤C∏y_i^s_i on the specified sector. A zero function is not roughly monomial.

api.name: BKT.RoughMonomial.positive
api.statement: A roughly monomial function is everywhere strictly positive.

api.name: BKT.RoughMonomial.productExponents
api.statement: Products add exponent vectors and multiply lower/upper constants.

api.name: BKT.RoughMonomial.inverseExponents
api.statement: Reciprocals negate exponents and invert/swap the comparison constants.

uses.how: Convert sector Hodge norm estimates into positive two-sided comparisons.

items.name: Roughly polynomial function
items.statement: A real function is roughly polynomial if it has an expression g/h with g∈O[x,y,y⁻¹] and h roughly monomial and nowhere zero on the sector. A complex function has roughly polynomial real and imaginary parts, or equivalently uses the complexified coefficient algebra with such real denominators.

api.name: BKT.RoughPolynomial.sum
api.statement: A sum of rough polynomials is a rough polynomial after multiplying the positive rough-monomial denominators.

api.name: BKT.RoughPolynomial.product
api.statement: A product is rough polynomial with product denominator.

api.name: BKT.RoughPolynomial.splitComplex
api.statement: Complex rough-polynomial entries have real and imaginary parts in the real class.

uses.how: Supply the algebraic-growth hypothesis essential to the curve test.

items.name: Closure laws for rough functions
items.statement: Roughly monomial functions are stable under products and reciprocals. Roughly polynomial functions form a ring and are stable under division by a roughly monomial function. The comparison constants and sector are retained in each operation.

items.name: Curve test for a global rough-polynomial bound
items.statement: For R ≥ 1 let Σ_n^R = {|Re z_i| < R, Im z_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ Im z_n > 1}; Σ_n is the part with 0 < Re z_i < 1. Let f be roughly polynomial and g roughly monomial on every Σ_n^R. Suppose that for every R, |f| ≤ C_{τ,R}|g| on every nonempty intersection of Σ_n^R with a complex affine curve α₁z₁+β₁=⋯=α_(n₀)z_(n₀)+β_(n₀), remaining coordinates fixed in H, for each 1≤n₀≤n, positive rational α_i and real β_i. Then one constant C bounds |f|/|g| on Σ_n. The R-uniform hypothesis repairs the printed proof (sourceIssues E2).
items.note: Repaired by the continuation (Claude Code cc-fb70e5): the printed proof's substitutions leave Σ_n (E2). The R-uniform hypothesis makes the induction valid.

items.name: Centered monodromy weight filtration
items.statement: For a nilpotent N on a finite-dimensional rational vector space, W(N) is the unique finite increasing filtration with N W_j⊂W_(j−2) and N^j:gr^W_j≅gr^W_(−j) for j≥0. It is centered at zero; for a weight-k limiting mixed Hodge structure the actual weights are shifted by k.

api.name: BKT.MonodromyWeightFiltration.lowersTwo
api.statement: N maps W_j into W_(j−2).

api.name: BKT.MonodromyWeightFiltration.gradedLefschetz
api.statement: N^j induces gr_j≃gr_(−j).

api.name: BKT.MonodromyWeightFiltration.weightShift
api.statement: For pure weight k use W_actual_l=W(N)_(l−k).

uses.how: Provide centered weight indices before constructing limiting mixed Hodge structures.

items.name: Constancy of monodromy weights on cone interiors
items.statement: For commuting nilpotents defining a polarized nilpotent orbit, every strictly positive combination of the nilpotents in a fixed nonempty face has the same centered monodromy weight filtration W(face). Faces with different sets of generators may have different filtrations.
items.note: Kashiwara’s statement was read; the original Cattani–Kaplan proof remains a gap.

items.name: Limiting mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: For the limiting F=Ψ(0) and N in the interior of the full monodromy cone, (F,W(N)[k]) is a mixed Hodge structure polarized in the nilpotent-orbit sense. The existing generic MixedHodgeStructure carrier is used; existence is a degeneration theorem.

items.name: Splittings adapted to all monodromy faces
items.statement: For M_j=N₁+⋯+N_j in an ordered sector, choose a finite complex splitting I^(p,q₁,…,q_n) recovering F^a by p≥a and the shifted W(M_j)_b by p+q_j≤b; also choose a rational splitting J_(s₁,…,s_n) recovering centered W(M_j)_b by s_j≤b. The two splittings serve distinct purposes and are not identified.

api.name: BKT.SimultaneousSplitting.recoverComplexFiltrations
api.statement: Summing I^(p,q₁,…,q_n) with p≥a or p+q_j≤b recovers F^a or shifted W_j,b.

api.name: BKT.SimultaneousSplitting.recoverRationalWeights
api.statement: Summing J_s with s_j≤b recovers the centered rational W_j,b.

api.name: BKT.SimultaneousSplitting.finiteSupport
api.statement: Only finitely many multi-indices have nonzero summands and their direct sum is the whole space.

uses.how: Supply nonzero vectors with a multi-weight and retain the rational/complex distinction.

items.name: Distributivity needed for simultaneous splittings
items.statement: For the limiting filtration F of a polarized nilpotent orbit and any nested sequence of nilpotent-generator subsets, F together with their monodromy weight filtrations is a distributive family and admits a common adapted splitting over C. The rational weight subfamily admits a rational splitting.
items.note: The selected proof was read; the real-split replacement and distributive-filtration algebra require exact supplier matching.

items.name: Asymptotic norm of a nonzero split flat vector
items.statement: For nonzero u∈J_(s₁,…,s_n)⊗C, h_z(u,u) is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of (y₁/y₂)^s₁⋯(y_(n−1)/y_n)^s_(n−1)y_n^s_n on the ordered sector after the standard shrinking. Constants may depend on u and the variation.
items.note: Kashiwara’s original p.870 was inspected as an image; the full proof and all its analytic inputs are not closed.

items.name: Asymptotic norm of a nilpotently twisted vector
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses and for nonzero u∈J_(s₁,…,s_n)⊗C, h_z(exp(Σz_iN_i)u,exp(Σz_iN_i)u) has the same monomial comparison as hodge-norm-asymptotic.

items.name: Holomorphic negative-Lie lift of the untwisted map
items.statement: For F=Ψ(0), the Deligne splitting of the limiting adjoint mixed Hodge structure gives a complement to the filtration stabilizer: the sum of pieces with first Hodge index p<0. On a sufficiently small polydisk there is a unique holomorphic v(q) in this complement, v(0)=0, with Ψ(q)=exp(v(q))F. Put g(q)=exp(v(q)) and γ(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)g(q(z)).

api.name: BKT.NegativeLieChart.localInverse
api.statement: On a sufficiently small neighborhood, exponentiating the negative complement and acting on F gives a local chart in the compact dual.

api.name: BKT.NegativeLieChart.movingFrame
api.statement: γ(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)g(q(z)) transports F to the varying filtration.

uses.how: Normalize the analytic correction so its Taylor decomposition has zero constant term.

items.name: Triangular form of the horizontal perturbation
items.statement: For negative-lie-chart, Griffiths transversality implies v(q)=Σ_i q_i v_i(q_i,…,q_n), with [N_j,v_i]=0 for j<i. Consequently g(q)=1+Σ_i q_i g_i(q), where g_i preserves every earlier monodromy filtration W(M_j), j<i.
items.note: The source gives this implication briefly; the coefficient-recursion proof and its uniform holomorphic bounds remain explicit tasks.

items.name: Exponential decay against ordered-sector powers
items.statement: Fix integer exponents on y_i,…,y_n with y_i≥⋯≥y_n≥1. The product e^(−4πy_i) times any such Laurent monomial tends uniformly to zero as y_n→∞. Negative powers are bounded by one and positive powers by a fixed power of y_i.

items.name: Comparison with the nilpotent-orbit frame
items.statement: For nonzero u in a fixed simultaneous weight component, h_z(γ(z)u,γ(z)u) is comparable to h_z(exp(Σz_iN_i)u,exp(Σz_iN_i)u) on a sufficiently deep ordered sector. The estimate is uniform over compact parameter sets with the stated splitting data.

items.name: Flag adapted to the Hodge filtration
items.statement: Choose an ordered basis w_i of the simultaneous complex splitting with decreasing first Hodge index p_i, and let K_i=span(w₁,…,w_i). The transported flag γK_i refines the varying Hodge filtration. Write B(u,v)=Q(u,conj v), which is generally indefinite. In pure weight k, B(v,u)=(−1)^k conjugate(B(u,v)); it is skew-Hermitian for odd k and i^kB is Hermitian.
items.note: E21 records the parity mislabel in the source. The determinant identities are sesquilinear, with the indicated phases.

api.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.refinesF
api.statement: The subflag at each Hodge-index cutoff equals that filtration step.

api.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.transportFlag
api.statement: γ maps K_i to the corresponding refined varying Hodge flag.

api.name: BKT.HodgeAdaptedFlag.gramConvention
api.statement: B(u,v)=Q(u,conj v) is linear in the first variable and need not be positive definite. Its symmetry parity is (−1)^k, not uniformly Hermitian.

uses.how: Use Hodge-ordered subspaces for nondegenerate polarization Gram determinants.

items.name: Nonvanishing of the adapted Gram minors
items.statement: For hodge-adapted-flag, B restricts nondegenerately to each γK_i. Its Gram determinant Δ_i=B(γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i),γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i)) is nonzero. Within each successive pure Hodge piece B has the scalar phase prescribed by the polarization.
items.note: Ordinary positive-inner-product Gram–Schmidt cannot be applied directly to the indefinite form B.

items.name: Gram determinant and projection identities
items.statement: Let wtilde_i be B-orthogonalized γw_i along the adapted flag and set Δ₀=1. Then B(wtilde_i,wtilde_i)=Δ_i/Δ_(i−1). For any u, B(u,wtilde_i)=B(γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_(i−1))∧u,γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i))/Δ_(i−1). The analogous formula holds with γu.

items.name: Rational expression for all Hodge matrix entries
items.statement: In a fixed flat complex basis, every h_z(u,v) lies in the complexified fraction algebra O(x,y). Decompose u,v in the B-orthogonal adapted basis; its ith contribution is i^(2p_i−k) B(u,wtilde_i)B(wtilde_i,v)/B(wtilde_i,wtilde_i).

items.name: Rough monomial norm on a simultaneous Hodge-weight piece
items.statement: For a nonzero fixed vector u in a simultaneous complex piece I^(p,q₁,…,q_n), its squared Hodge norm is roughly monomial on a sufficiently deep ordered sector. The corresponding centered weight exponents are obtained by shifting p+q_j by the pure weight.

items.name: Rough monomial norm of the transported vector
items.statement: For nonzero u in a simultaneous complex piece, the squared norm h_z(γ(z)u,γ(z)u) is roughly monomial, including the determinant vectors of the adapted flag in the induced exterior-power variations.

items.name: Rough polynomial pairing of split vectors
items.statement: For u and v in simultaneous complex pieces, the real and imaginary parts of h_z(u,v) are roughly polynomial. Zero vectors give the zero function and require no roughly monomial assertion.

items.name: Rough polynomial Hodge form
items.statement: For any fixed u,v in the complex flat fibre, h_z(u,v) has roughly polynomial real and imaginary parts on an ordered sector after shrinking.

items.name: Reduced positive form with an ordered basis
items.statement: For a positive definite real symmetric form b, ordered rational basis e and C>0, call b (e,C)-reduced if |b(e_i,e_j)|<C b(e_i,e_i) for all i,j; b(e_i,e_i)<C b(e_j,e_j) for i<j; and ∏_i b(e_i,e_i)<C det(b in e). Rational bases are converted to lattice bases only with explicit denominator and finite-index changes.

api.name: BKT.ReducedForm.offDiagonal
api.statement: Reducedness gives |b_ij|<C b_ii for every ordered pair.

api.name: BKT.ReducedForm.diagonalOrder
api.statement: For i<j, b_ii<C b_jj; this condition depends on the ordering of the basis.

api.name: BKT.ReducedForm.permutationRepair
api.statement: After obtaining uniform off-diagonal and determinant bounds, sort diagonal lengths; one of finitely many basis permutations then satisfies full reducedness with a suitable uniform constant.

uses.how: Separate off-diagonal bounds, ordering and determinant bounds before choosing finite permutations.

items.name: Reduced forms and Siegel sets
items.statement: For a fixed ordered rational basis e and C, the set of (e,C)-reduced positive forms is semialgebraic and contained in a Siegel set of the positive-form symmetric space for its chosen compact. Conversely each such Siegel set lies in a reduced-form set for some basis and constant.
items.note: The quoted original Klingen reduction proof remains a source-audit gap.

items.name: Basis change with determinant control and finite ordering
items.statement: Fix real bases e,e′ of an n-dimensional real vector space, n≥1, C′≥1 and C≥1. Suppose b is (e′,C′)-reduced and ∏b(e_i,e_i)≤C det(b in e). With the constants of basis-change-offdiagonal, let K=C′³ max_(i,j)(L_iL_j/m_i²). For any C″>max(1,C,K), some permutation σ ordering the b(e_i,e_i) increasingly makes b (σe,C″)-reduced. The finite set of possible σ is independent of b. Rational bases are the arithmetic specialization.
items.locator: §4.5, p.18, basis-transfer assertion with explicit ordering qualification
items.note: Quantitative proof supplied by codex-a71f92. This resolves the basis-transfer portion of G5, not the finite boundary-chart or analytic-input portions. E3 remains an unreviewed correction to the printed fixed-order assertion.

items.name: Bounded product of adapted diagonal norms
items.statement: For a rational basis adapted to the simultaneous centered monodromy weight filtrations, the product of its squared Hodge norms is bounded by a constant times the determinant of the Hodge form. Centered weights cancel in the top exterior power.

items.name: One-variable period lift lies in a Siegel set
items.statement: For a unipotent local polarized period map and any R,η>0, its lift on {|Re z|≤R, Im z≥η} lies in one rational Siegel set for the compatible Hodge compact data.
items.note: The corollary and immediate proof were read; the preceding SL₂ theorem is still an imported proof leaf.

items.name: Faithful representation compatible with the Hodge compact
items.statement: Choose a faithful rational polarized Hodge representation of the semisimple group used for D, possibly replacing the adjoint presentation by an appropriate central cover or by its adjoint representation. The induced map to the positive-form symmetric space has compatible maximal compacts and Cartan involutions; its preimage fibres include the compact K/M directions.
items.locator: §4.5, passage to positive definite forms; erratum§§1.4–1.5
items.note: This is an explicit representation/central-cover adapter, not an assumed embedding of every adjoint Mumford–Tate group into GL of the original fibre.

items.name: Reducedness along each rational-slope curve
items.statement: On every curve used by rational-curve-test, pullback of the local variation, after clearing rational slope denominators, has one-variable unipotent monodromy. Schmid’s theorem and the faithful representation give reducedness in some fixed curve-dependent rational basis; determinant control transfers the off-diagonal bounds to the chosen simultaneous basis.

items.name: Uniform reducedness up to finitely many basis permutations
items.statement: On a sufficiently deep ordered sector, the Hodge forms satisfy all off-diagonal reducedness bounds in one adapted rational basis with a single constant. Sorting its finitely many basis vectors pointwise gives finitely many reduced-form sets covering the image.
items.locator: §4.5, main claim with explicit finite permutations

items.name: Finite Siegel containment for a local period lift
items.statement: Let a polarized integral variation on (Δ*)^n have unipotent monodromy and lift Φtilde:H^n→D. For each R,η>0 its image on H^n_(R,η) is contained in a finite union of rational Siegel sets of D, all for the canonical Hodge compact. The multivariable assertion is finite union, not one set.
items.note: Uniform estimates with auxiliary parameters and the face-cover step remain an explicit proof interface.

items.name: Definability on a smaller punctured polydisk
items.statement: For a polarized integral variation on a punctured polydisk, there is a smaller radius ρ>0 such that its period map restricted to (Δ*_ρ)^n is R_an,exp-definable in the canonical target structure. Products with sufficiently small unpunctured disks and finite quasi-unipotent covers are included.
items.locator: Theorem4.1 as used after the shrinking in §4.2
items.note: The printed whole-open-polydisk formulation is false (sourceIssues E1); see local-outer-boundary-obstruction.

items.name: Definability of the global period map
items.statement: For a pure polarized integral variation on a smooth complex quasi-projective S, its holomorphic period map to the associated torsion-free arithmetic Hodge manifold, with the canonical compact-dependent structure, is R_an,exp-definable relative to the algebraic definable structure on S.

items.name: Why shrinking the local polydisk is necessary
items.statement: The assertion that every local period map on the entire open punctured unit disk is definable is false. Let f(z)=exp(−(1+z)/(1−z)) and τ(z)=2i+εf(z) for sufficiently small ε>0. This gives a weight-one polarized integral variation with trivial monodromy and image in an injective uniformization chart. The fibre f=e^(−1) contains z_n=2πin/(2+2πin), n≠0, accumulating at the outer boundary 1, so it is not o-minimal-definable.
items.locator: Audit example for Theorem4.1 and its explicit shrinking in the proof
items.note: Recorded as sourceIssues E1: printed Theorem 4.1 claims the whole punctured polydisk. This is not in the official erratum and is not a counterexample to Theorem 1.3 on an algebraic base.

items.name: Canonical structure on the symmetric space quotient
items.statement: Let X be the G-homogeneous space of maximal compact subgroups. Transporting the fixed-K structure on Γ\G/K along gK↦gKg⁻¹ gives a semialgebraic structure on Γ\X independent of K. More generally an equivariant map Y→X specifies compatible choices at every point of a homogeneous G-space Y.

items.name: Definable complex analytic Chow theorem
items.statement: If S is a complex algebraic variety and Z⊂S^an is a closed complex analytic subset definable in an o-minimal expansion of R_an, then Z is algebraic. Here it suffices to take S smooth and quasi-projective. Closedness and compatibility with the algebraic definable structure are hypotheses.
items.locator: §§4.6–5; [PS09] Theorem4.5; restated in the paper as Theorem 4.13 (Peterzil–Starchenko)

items.name: A holomorphic map with algebraic graph is regular
items.statement: For smooth complex algebraic S and a separated complex algebraic Y, a holomorphic map f:S^an→Y^an whose graph is algebraic comes from a regular algebraic map. The projection of its reduced algebraic graph to S is an isomorphism.
items.note: Precise algebraic/analytic comparison supplier and full proof still require decomposition; no properness of S is assumed.

items.name: Arithmetic and algebraic definability on Hermitian quotients
items.statement: For a torsion-free arithmetic quotient of a Hermitian symmetric domain, the identity between the fixed-canonical-K arithmetic definable structure and its Baily–Borel algebraic definable structure is R_an,exp-definable. This is not in general R_an-definable.
items.note: Acquire KUY16 proof and establish that its use here is independent of the Borel algebraicity theorem being reproved; do not silently identify the two structures.

items.name: Borel algebraicity via period-map definability
items.statement: Every holomorphic map from a smooth complex algebraic variety to a torsion-free arithmetic quotient of a Hermitian symmetric domain is algebraic with respect to its algebraic quotient structure.

items.name: Proper special Hodge subvarieties
items.statement: A special Hodge subvariety relevant to the exceptional Hodge locus is the image of an arithmetic Hodge morphism from a Hodge subdatum with strictly smaller generic Mumford–Tate group (allowing connected components and rational translates). The exceptional qualifier excludes the identity image of the generic Hodge datum.

api.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.subdatumImage
api.statement: Form the image of the compatible arithmetic Hodge morphism at the chosen levels.

api.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.properGenericCondition
api.statement: The defining exceptional datum has strictly smaller generic Mumford–Tate group.

api.name: BKT.SpecialHodgeSubvariety.rationalTranslate
api.statement: Rational translates and connected arithmetic components are included in the same countable source family.

uses.how: Make the exceptional locus a countable collection of proper special images.

items.name: Closed analytic images of Hodge morphisms
items.statement: An arithmetic Hodge morphism associated to a Hodge subdatum has proper map onto its image, and its image is a closed complex analytic subvariety of the target Hodge manifold. Its source and target are taken at compatible arithmetic levels.
items.note: The precise properness and analytic image inputs have not been fully source-decomposed; they cannot be replaced by definability alone.

items.name: Definability of each special Hodge subvariety
items.statement: Each special Hodge subvariety is semialgebraic-definable in the canonical arithmetic structure on the target Hodge manifold. This does not assert algebraicity of a generally nonalgebraic Hodge manifold.

items.name: Countable supply of exceptional Hodge subdata
items.statement: For a fixed rational polarized Hodge datum there are countably many rational tensor conditions and rational Hodge subdata that can cut out exceptional Mumford–Tate groups, including their rational translates and arithmetic connected components. Their special images cover the exceptional Hodge locus.
items.note: The tensor-stabilizer/Hodge-subdatum correspondence and component enumeration are still prerequisite proof leaves.

items.name: Algebraicity of each special-locus pullback
items.statement: For a pure polarized integral variation over smooth complex quasi-projective S with period map Φ, the preimage of any special Hodge subvariety is a closed algebraic subvariety of S.

items.name: Algebraicity of the exceptional Hodge locus
items.statement: The exceptional Hodge locus of a pure polarized integral variation over a smooth complex quasi-projective variety is a countable union of closed irreducible algebraic subvarieties. Each special-image pullback has finitely many algebraic irreducible components. The countable union need not itself be definable or closed.

items.name: Finiteness of definable connected components
items.statement: Every definable subset of R^n in an o-minimal expansion of the real field has finitely many connected components, each definable. This extends to finite definable atlases.

items.name: Existing planned normal-crossing compactification
items.statement: A smooth complex quasi-projective variety has a smooth projective compactification whose reduced boundary is a simple normal-crossing divisor.

items.name: Proper holomorphic image theorem
items.statement: The image of a proper holomorphic map of complex analytic spaces is a closed complex analytic subset of the target.

items.name: Uniform arithmetic lattices have no nontrivial unipotents
items.statement: A cocompact lattice in the real points of a semisimple group contains no nonidentity unipotent element.
items.note: Original Raghunathan proof not acquired in this checkpoint.

items.name: Restricted-analytic definability for a compact Hodge target
items.statement: If the arithmetic Hodge target of a pure polarized integral variation on smooth complex quasi-projective S is compact, then its period map is R_an-definable. At a torsion-free target level, finite local monodromy in the adjoint target is trivial; after the needed finite level cover the period map extends across a normal-crossing compactification.
items.note: Finite global level-cover and extension details remain to be decomposed; no claim of a compact-target proof independent of the Hodge degeneration inputs.

items.name: Existing Cholesky reconstruction
items.statement: For a positive-definite real symmetric n×n matrix A, the pinned Cholesky factor L is lower triangular with positive diagonal and satisfies L Lᵀ=A.
items.note: The factor, triangularity and reconstruction are already implemented; no new Cholesky construction is planned.

items.name: Existing adjugate inverse identity
items.statement: For a square matrix A over a commutative ring, its nonsingular inverse is Ring.inverse(det A) times adjugate A. Over R with det A≠0 this is (det A)⁻¹ adjugate A.
items.note: Read with the singular-case convention; consumers below have positive determinant.

items.name: Determinant-controlled lower bound for a coordinate
items.statement: Let B be a positive-definite real symmetric n×n matrix, n≥1, d_k=B_kk, and D≥1 with ∏_k d_k≤D det B. For any real coordinate vector a and any k, aᵀBa≥a_k² d_k/D.
items.note: Derived planning lemma, not asserted as a separately numbered result of the source.

items.name: Quantitative off-diagonal transfer in a fixed basis
items.statement: Let n≥1 and B be the Gram matrix in the ordered basis e′ of a positive-definite real form b. Suppose C′≥1, |B_ab|≤C′d_a for all a,b, d_a≤C′d_b for a<b, and ∏d_a≤C′det B, where d_a=B_aa. Let e_i=∑_a A_ai e′_a be another fixed real basis. Put k_i=max{a:A_ai≠0}, m_i=|A_(k_i),i| and L_i=∑_a|A_ai|. Then |b(e_i,e_j)|≤C′³ L_i L_j m_i⁻² b(e_i,e_i) for all i,j. The change matrix is fixed; the bound is uniform in b.
items.note: Derived planning lemma, not asserted as a separately numbered result of the source.

items.name: Definability of buffered analytic chart transitions
items.statement: Let φ_i:U_i→X and φ_j:U_j→X be compatible real analytic corner charts. Let B_i⊂U_i and B_j⊂U_j be relatively open semialgebraic boxes whose closures are compact subsets of the respective original chart domains. Then the graph of φ_j⁻¹φ_i on B_i∩φ_i⁻¹(φ_j(B_j)) is globally subanalytic, hence R_an-definable.
items.locator: Published Proposition A.2, pp.935–936; explicit compact-graph repair of its transition step
items.note: Derived planning lemma, not asserted as a separately numbered result of the source.

items.name: Properness of the finite relation on Siegel closures
items.statement: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff semialgebraic space with a group acting by semialgebraic homeomorphisms. Let C₁,…,C_r⊂X be closed semialgebraic subsets. Assume for each ordered pair only finitely many group elements have γC_i∩C_j≠∅. Then on C=⊔C_i the orbit relation E⊂C×C is semialgebraic, closed, and both coordinate projections E→C are proper.
items.locator: Published §3.1, p.926; expanded proof of the proper-relation assertion
items.note: Derived planning lemma, not asserted as a separately numbered result of the source.
